newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DIAMOND PRODUCTION SOARS IN FIVE YEARS.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DIAMOND PRODUCTION SOARS IN FIVE YEARS.

text.p: Diamond production in Zimbabwe has soared since the country's first mine started operating in 1992, with good prospects for further growth this decade, an industry official said on Friday.

Kevin Dabinett, general manager at Auridiam Zimbabwe Private Ltd, which owns the River Ranch diamond mine in southern Zimbabwe, said the mine produced over 474,130 carats of diamonds in 1996, earning Z$91 million in exports, compared with an initial 23,870 carats in 1992 which fetched in Z$9.4 million.
Auridiam expects to produce 565,760 carats of the mineral in 1997, earning between Z$120 million and Z$140 million.
Dabinett said while the River Ranch was currently was the sole diamond mine in the southern African country, other prospectors were set to join in the race within the next few years.
"There is very good potential for other diamond mines in Zimbabwe within the next 10 years," he told Reuters.
President of Zimbabwe's chamber of mines John Nixon also thinks the future for diamond mining in Zimbabwe looks "cautiously bright".
"I don't believe that the country will come up empty handed from all this prospecting," Nixon said.

Two thirds of Zimbabwe is covered with the craton-type soil in which can be found the kimberlite rock which houses diamonds, and mining officials say kimberlite constitutes about one percent of the country's land.
Besides Auridiam, other prospectors include Trillion Zimbabwe Ltd , Reunion , BHP , and Kimberlite Searches owned by South Africa's De Beers .
Trillion's exploration manager Pat Donovan says his company has made finds in the western part of the country bordering Botswana, and could be producing diamonds within the next three to five years.
"I do believe there's potential there but we're still working out the logistics before we can go into production," Donovan said.
